title: channel-reshaper: INT8→FP8 hybrid kernel and prefetch orchestrator for steady KV-cache throughput
author: Arjun Patel
description: Motivation: INT8 optimized kernels achieve great throughput for typical attention workloads, but we observed two classes of production regressions: 1) per-channel scale drift across fused attention+proj paths that causes extra requant/dequant overhead; 2) KV-cache prefetching that becomes misaligned with continuous-batching windows under variable request sizes, causing GPU memory jitter and tail latency spikes. This PR introduces a two-part change to mitigate both issues while preserving compatibility: (a) a channel-reshaper kernel that reorders per-head/channel layout into contiguous vectors for vectorized requant/dequant and fused smoothquant paths; (b) a prefetch orchestrator in the scheduling layer that ties KV prefetch windows to continuous-batching boundaries and applies a small amortized FP8 fallback when long sequences would otherwise trigger costly per-token dequant ramps. Summary of changes: - New runtime kernel: server/runtime/quant/channel_reshaper.cpp/h — implements a low-overhead channel reordering that enables in-place per-channel scale application and reduces memory traffic for dequant fusion. The kernel targets AVX512/WMMA microkernels and has a fallback path for non-vectorized devices. - Hybrid quant path: server/runtime/quant/hybrid_fp8_int8_adapter.* — introduces a thin adapter that accepts INT8-packed weights and emits a transient FP8-shadow during long sequences to avoid repeated INT8→FP32→INT8 reconversions; this is controlled by a per-layer heuristic. - Scheduler integration: server/runtime/scheduler/prefetch_orchestrator.cpp/h — ties KV prefetch windows with continuous batching windows, adds an LRU-protected prefetch budget per-GPU, and delays aggressive prefetch for microbatch coalescing when expected batch multiplexing is high. - Runtime hooks and tests: server/runtime/tests/quant_perf_benchmarks.py, server/runtime/tests/prefetch_scheduler_tests.cc — microbenchmarks for LLaMA-2-70b, Mistral-7B, and a small-flavor transformer showing stable p50/p95 latency and higher sustained throughput. - Docs & rollout: docs/notes/quant-prefetch-design.md, tools/flags/quant_flags.toml — rollout gate via runtime flag quant.experimental.channel_reshaper and scheduler.prefer_coalesce. Design tradeoffs and notes: - The reshaper reduces stray loads during fused requant by making per-channel scales contiguous; on our internal microbench it reduced attention kernel memory traffic by ~18% on A100 and produced a 9–12% throughput gain for INT8 end-to-end generation in 1–8 token response scenarios. - The hybrid FP8 adapter is intentionally conservative: it flips to FP8-shadow only when expected sequence length > 1024 OR when the per-layer scale variance exceeds a threshold over warm-up tokens; this avoids quality regressions for short-lived requests. - Prefetch orchestrator prevents double-prefetch when continuous-batcher already holds recent KV slots and reduces p95 latency spikes by ~14% in mixed-size synthetic workloads. Testing and verification: - Unit tests for the reshaper correctness (round-trip quant/dequant) and scheduler invariants. - Microbench harness with perf counters for bytes-read/bytes-written, observed KV hit/miss rates, and per-token latency histograms. - End-to-end smoke tests against the hosted API with the new flags enabled. Checklist: - [x] Channel reshaper kernel implemented and unit-tested - [x] Hybrid FP8 adapter implemented with fallback heuristics - [x] Scheduler integration and budget accounting - [x] Microbench results included - [x] Runtime flag gating and docs - [x] Fix race discovered in early review (see conversation) - [x] CI green after rerun Migration/rollout plan: start behind runtime flags in Dedicated canaries for 2 weeks, then enable for low-risk customers, monitor token-level cost/latency dashboards (Console). If metrics regress, scheduler.prefer_coalesce=false and quant.experimental.channel_reshaper=false to revert without restart.

review_thread: Sofia Kim: Looks solid overall. Two asks: 1) add an alignment check for non-AVX512 paths, 2) please add a smoke test for quantized model output parity (small numeric tolerance).
Arjun Patel: Responded - added fallback_scalar.cc for non-AVX512 alignment checks and added quant_perf_benchmarks.py with tolerance check. See commit d5b8e12.
Marcus Bell: Prefetch budget logic seems racy when multiple batchers touch the same GPU; can you add an atomic fence or use the gpu allocator epoch?
Arjun Patel: Found the race - budget accounting used a non-atomic counter. Converted to std::atomic and moved budget map under the gpu epoch lock. Fixed in e7f3b53.
Rita Chen: CI flaked on the integration tests (gpu allocator OOM) — reran CI after changing the bench harness to allocate smaller prefetch windows. CI is green now.

Marcus Bell: Approved after verifying microbench numbers on A100 and internal canary cluster.
LGTM (squash)
merge_commit: m7c9d4a: squash-merge channel reshaper + prefetch orchestrator
release_notes: Introduce channel reshaper kernel and a prefetch orchestrator to improve INT8 runtime throughput and reduce p95 latency spikes. Gate behind quant.experimental.channel_reshaper and scheduler.prefer_coalesce flags. Expected improvements: +9–12% throughput for short responses, ~14% reduction in p95 mixed-workload latency. Rollout behind flags for canary first.
notes: Follow-up backlog: 1) investigate extending reshaper to fused linear projection + RMSnorm fusion, 2) add telemetry for per-layer FP8-shadow activations, 3) evaluate memory tax on smaller GPU sizes (T4/GPU).
